query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Alloying the CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy with ~10 at% Ag will yield an in situ Ag-rich phase that segregates to sliding contacts, forming a continuous, low-shear-strength tribofilm and thereby reducing coefficient of friction and wear rate across 25 °C–800 °C relative to the baseline CoCrFeNi alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast single-phase fcc CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy.
generation.intervention: Substitutional addition of 10 at% Ag to form a CoCrFeNiAg10 high-entropy alloy.
generation.conditions: Dry sliding in ambient air (20–30% RH), normal load 5–20 N, sliding speed 0.1–0.5 m/s, temperature range 25 °C to 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: An Ag-rich second phase that under shear migrates to the surface and coalesces into a lubricious film.
generation.mechanism: Under sliding contact, soft Ag phase smears and wets the wear track, creating a continuous low-shear film stable up to 800 °C owing to Ag’s high melting point and oxidation resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to baseline CoCrFeNi, CoCrFeNiAg10 will exhibit a lower coefficient of friction and reduced wear rate at all tested temperatures from 25 °C to 800 °C.
generation.baseline: Baseline CoCrFeNi shows friction increasing from ≈0.5 at room temperature to ≈0.6+ at 800 °C with wear rates rising accordingly due to oxide-dominated wear.
generation.boundary: Valid for sliding in air (20–50% RH), under normal loads ≤20 N, sliding speeds of 0.1–0.5 m/s, and temperatures between 25 °C and 800 °C; untested outside these ranges.
generation.uncertainty: High – direct prior studies of Ag additions in CoCrFeNi across the full 25 °C–800 °C range are lacking.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeNiAg10 alloys under identical processing. Conduct ball-on-disc sliding tests in air at 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C using a 10 N normal load and 0.1 m/s sliding speed. Compare friction and wear.
measurements: Coefficient of friction vs. sliding distance at each temperature
SEM-EDS phase and composition mapping of wear tracks
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If CoCrFeNiAg10 does not show ≥10% reduction in both coefficient of friction and wear rate relative to CoCrFeNi at three or more of the tested temperatures, the hypothesis is falsified.
